correctness.rationale: For the exact Petersen matching complex, a 14-edge spanning tree and 145 triangle relations kill every fundamental-group edge generator; a transposition fixes a matching-complex vertex and its conjugates normally generate S5, so Armstrong proves the quotient π1=0. The reconstructed 125 quotient orbit-chain CW cells have exact integral boundaries with d²=0. The standalone checker performs 62 valid ±1 chain cancellations leaving one C0 and no other chains; this proves vanishing of all reduced integral homology, including torsion. Hurewicz and Whitehead then give contractibility. The checker replays to the byte-identical supplied output.

value.rationale: The original Petersen matching complex has nontrivial second and third homology, while its full quotient was known only to be rationally acyclic. The precise remaining question—whether symmetry creates integral torsion or leaves a contractible quotient—is mathematically natural for this canonical highly symmetric graph. The complete integral homotopy classification closes that specific gap, with a reproducible exact certificate, not merely a rational or numerical approximation.
